purpose: Typed inventory of internal organs and external artifacts. This catalog does not grant execution, credentials, approval, or authority.
authority_invariant: CK-NEXUS Core alone owns L3 authority. Every external provider, tool, plugin, connector, skill package, workflow engine, knowledge source, parser, store, and observer has authority_scope NONE.

artifacts.integration_point: creator_app/control_plane + council_authority + policy/evidence contracts
artifacts.notes: Single authority. No external framework or model may override it. Production remains NO-GO until release gates are satisfied.

artifacts.name: Agent Skills Open Specification
artifacts.integration_point: creator_app/agnes_skills.py + creator_app/skills/agnes/SKILL.md (format and metadata conformance review only)
artifacts.notes: Open format donated to the Agentic AI Foundation on 2026-10-22. Anthropic reports more than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, have integrated the format. No GitHub Releases were published as checked on 2026-11-09; pin a reviewed commit SHA rather than relying on a version tag. Experimental allowed-tools is not a security boundary. Do not execute bundled scripts without source, license, checksum, permission and sandbox review.
artifacts.upstream_version: living specification; no formal tagged release observed on 2026-11-09
artifacts.maintenance_signal: Anthropic announced donation to the Linux Foundation AAIF on 2026-10-22; repository has no published Releases at review time.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Format-level only; no runtime package required. Loader compatibility must be checked per AGNES client.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: No runtime dependency for reading the specification. Optional skills may bundle arbitrary scripts, references and assets.
artifacts.permission_scope: Skill instructions grant no credentials or authority. A client may execute bundled scripts if configured; quarantine and review scripts before activation.
artifacts.latency_cost: Low baseline cost; progressive disclosure loads metadata first and full instructions/resources only on activation.
artifacts.security_notes: Treat third-party skills as untrusted content. Validate SKILL.md metadata; pin repository commit and file hashes; inspect scripts and allowed-tools. This field is not a replacement for CK-NEXUS policy.

artifacts.name: Promptfoo LLM Evaluation and Red-Team CLI
artifacts.integration_point: Optional isolated CI evaluation job consuming redacted staging fixtures; no production request-path integration
artifacts.notes: Official latest release observed: 0.125.1 (2026-10-25). Promptfoo states it is now part of OpenAI and remains MIT-licensed. Official docs list 157 red-team plugins, including coding-agent tests for repository prompt injection, terminal-output injection, secret reads, sandbox escapes, verifier sabotage and delayed CI exfiltration. Some Community-edition plugins use remote inference; inspect the 🌐 marker and data path before selecting them.
artifacts.maintenance_signal: Official GitHub release 0.125.1 on 2026-10-25; official installation documentation updated 2026-11-07.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Node.js >=22.22.0 for npm/npx; Node.js 24 LTS recommended.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: 74 direct runtime dependencies and 52 devDependencies in upstream package.json at review time; installed size not measured. Use a dedicated CI container/worker, not the resource-constrained CK-NEXUS VPS.
artifacts.permission_scope: Runs with invoking OS-user permissions and reads configured project/test inputs. Configured providers receive selected prompts and test data. Some Community red-team plugins require Promptfoo-hosted remote inference; review the globe marker and data path. Local UI/MCP interfaces can read configs, run evals, write outputs and invoke providers; do not expose them to untrusted networks.
artifacts.latency_cost: Community plan is free and lists up to 10,000 red-team probes/month. Runtime scales with test cases, strategies, retries and model graders; provider API and remote-inference charges vary. Apply per-run time/token/cost limits and prefer approved local models where suitable.
artifacts.security_notes: Treat configs, scripts, providers, datasets and pull-request content as untrusted code/data. Some remote-only plugins (including SSRF, BOLA/BFLA and indirect-prompt-injection tests) use Promptfoo-hosted generation. PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_REMOTE_GENERATION disables supported remote-generation fallbacks but is not an egress firewall and does not disable all telemetry/provider traffic. Run in an isolated container/VM with least-privilege credentials and restricted egress; use synthetic/redacted fixtures. Local UI/MCP is not a security boundary.

artifacts.name: UK AI Security Institute Inspect AI
artifacts.integration_point: Optional isolated CI benchmark/evaluation worker; results ingested as evidence candidates, never as policy authority
artifacts.notes: PyPI latest release observed: 0.3.288 (2026-11-07), uploaded with Trusted Publishing provenance. The 35.6 MB wheel and broad dependency surface make it a separate CI benchmark worker, not a production/VPS dependency.
artifacts.maintenance_signal: PyPI 0.3.288 uploaded 2026-11-07 with Trusted Publishing provenance verified by PyPI against the official GitHub repository and release workflow.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Python >=3.11; supports model providers, task/scorer extensions and Docker sandboxes.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: Large distribution and broad Python dependency surface: the 0.3.288 wheel is 35.6 MB; dependencies include cloud SDKs, FastAPI, numpy, fsspec/s3fs, pydantic, textual and tiktoken. Prefer a separate CI worker.
artifacts.permission_scope: Evaluation tools can execute shell/Python work in a configured sandbox. Only calls routed through the sandbox interface are isolated; provisioning a container alone does not sandbox arbitrary evaluator code.
artifacts.latency_cost: Runtime depends on task/sample count, model calls, concurrency, retries and sandbox startup. Model API usage and worker compute are metered; set explicit task/sample time, message, token and cost limits.
artifacts.security_notes: Do not run untrusted task code or third-party evaluation packages with production credentials. Enable a sandbox for tools that execute arbitrary code, restrict egress, and preserve eval logs and exact task/model/config versions.

artifacts.name: Microsoft Playwright MCP Server
artifacts.integration_point: Optional isolated browser worker behind Connector Fabric; compare with existing CK-NEXUS browser automation wrapper before adding a second adapter
artifacts.notes: Official release 0.0.84 observed on 2026-10-31. Adds isolated browser contexts and URL-parameter redaction. Upstream explicitly says Playwright MCP is not a security boundary; its README suggests CLI plus Skills when token efficiency matters for coding agents.
artifacts.maintenance_signal: Signed GitHub release 0.0.84 on 2026-10-31; npm metadata reports Apache-2.0 and the same version.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Node.js >=18; the v0.0.84 release pins Playwright 1.65.0-alpha-2026-10-30. Inspected VPS Node.js v24.22.1 meets the engine requirement, but the package is not installed or runtime-verified.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: Two direct runtime dependencies (playwright and playwright-core), but the release pins an alpha Playwright build; browser engines and native OS libraries add substantial disk/RAM use. No installed-size measurement. Inspected VPS has 2.2 GiB free disk and about 438 MiB RAM available; do not install there.
artifacts.permission_scope: Browser navigation, accessibility snapshots, clicking/typing, page JavaScript, downloads/uploads and optional cookies/storage/network/devtools. Can mutate authenticated websites and expose session state. browser_run_code_unsafe executes arbitrary JavaScript in the MCP server process and is RCE-equivalent; deny it. Restrict hosts, egress, workspace roots and tool capabilities; bind to loopback and use isolated contexts.
artifacts.latency_cost: Browser startup and page/action round trips add latency; CPU/RAM and model tokens are workload-dependent. MCP has a broad schema; CLI plus Skills can be more token-efficient for coding-agent flows.
artifacts.security_notes: Upstream says this is not a security boundary. browser_run_code_unsafe is explicitly RCE-equivalent; deny it at the client policy. allowed-origins defaults to allow all and origin filters do not protect redirects or form a security boundary. Do not expose the server publicly, attach logged-in profiles, use --no-sandbox or enable unrestricted file access for untrusted pages. Run in a separately sandboxed container with no host secrets/mounts and enforced egress controls; URL redaction is convenience only.

artifacts.name: Official Model Context Protocol Server Registry
artifacts.integration_point: Read-only Connector Fabric discovery source; ingest metadata into a review queue only, never auto-install or auto-authorize a listed server
artifacts.license: MIT for legacy contributions; Apache-2.0 for new code/spec contributions; CC-BY-4.0 for documentation during the licensing transition (verify per file)
artifacts.notes: Official hosted registry; latest repository release v1.8.8 (2026-11-06). Public read API requires no publishing credentials. The registry is a metadata index, not a package host or code-security scanner. API documentation still describes preview status; breaking changes/data resets may occur. Public security advisories include SSRF, stored XSS, open redirect, OIDC token replay and an OCI ownership-check issue; verify advisory status and release commit before relying on the service.
artifacts.maintenance_signal: Signed release v1.8.8 on 2026-11-06; active repository with ongoing production/staging deployment and dependency updates.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Read-only HTTP REST API and OpenAPI metadata; no local runtime dependency. Publishing requires namespace ownership verification through GitHub OAuth/OIDC or DNS/HTTP proof.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: None for hosted read-only API consumption. Self-hosting requires Go, Docker/ko, PostgreSQL and operations; upstream states the official codebase is not designed for self-hosting.
artifacts.permission_scope: Public metadata reads do not require credentials. Publishing requires namespace ownership proof. Registry membership does not grant the listed MCP server credentials or execution permissions.
artifacts.latency_cost: Network/API pagination latency; no per-call public read price stated in the reviewed docs. Self-hosting adds database, container and operations cost.
artifacts.security_notes: Namespace and package-ownership validation improve publisher identity but do not scan or attest the server code. Registry documentation delegates package scanning to package registries/downstream aggregators. Review the five published advisories (including moderate SSRF and stored XSS); do not treat registry inclusion as safety approval. Validate package signatures, hashes, dependencies, runtime permissions and network egress independently.

artifacts.name: OpenSandbox Agent Sandbox Runtime
artifacts.integration_point: Future separate sandbox worker behind CK-NEXUS Connector Fabric; compare against the existing Linux namespace/cgroup sandbox and sandbox_executor before any adapter or deployment
artifacts.notes: Official Agentic AI Foundation project. Latest stable release 1.2.0 (2026-10-27; signed); latest upstream pre-release 1.2.1-rc.1 (2026-11-04; images only, SDK/CLI packages deferred to the 1.2.1 stable release). Main branch commit c00e5ad was updated 2026-11-09. Platform-level Docker/Kubernetes runtime, not a lightweight MCP adapter. Keep discovery-only until a separate worker and hardened policy profile are available.
artifacts.maintenance_signal: Signed stable 1.2.0 release on 2026-10-27; signed 1.2.1-rc.1 pre-release on 2026-11-04; official main commit c00e5ad updated 2026-11-09. Security policy supports only latest release and main.
artifacts.runtime_compatibility: Server requires Python >=3.10; inspected VPS Python 3.12.3 and active Docker 29.1.3 satisfy basic prerequisites. kubectl, runsc, kata-runtime and firecracker are absent; OpenSandbox packages are not installed. Current docs/chart require Kubernetes >=1.21.1, Helm 3 and kubectl; release-1.2.0 server/pyproject still describes Kubernetes as planned, so verify the exact server/chart pair before choosing that mode. Secure runtime must be explicitly configured; default runc is not a strong isolation runtime.
artifacts.dependency_footprint: High infrastructure footprint: server/pyproject.toml declares 19 direct runtime dependencies (Docker, FastAPI/Starlette, Kubernetes client, OpenTelemetry, PostgreSQL/Redis clients, gRPC and protobuf); deployment adds controller, ingress gateway and optional fast-sandbox components. No installed-size measurement. Not suitable for the current 2.2 GiB-free VPS.
artifacts.permission_scope: Server API key is optional; an empty key disables authentication, so set it before exposure. Docker mode requires access to the Docker daemon; Kubernetes mode requires cluster RBAC for sandbox CRDs/workloads and controllers. The API can create/delete sandboxes, execute commands, read/write sandbox files and configure egress. The default empty storage.allowed_host_paths rejects host bind mounts; add only narrow explicit paths if required. Multi-tenancy requires Kubernetes namespaces; Docker mode is unsupported.
artifacts.latency_cost: Self-hosted Apache-2.0 software; no per-request SaaS price is stated. Cost is host/cluster compute, storage, network, secure-runtime operations and maintenance. Upstream secure-runtime guide estimates startup overhead of about 10-50 ms/50 MB for gVisor, 500 ms/20-50 MB for Kata QEMU and 125 ms/5 MB for Kata Firecracker; these are vendor estimates, not CK-NEXUS benchmarks.
artifacts.security_notes: Default runc provides process-level cgroups only; configure gVisor, Kata or Firecracker explicitly for stronger isolation. Empty server.api_key means unauthenticated API access. Kubernetes sandboxes can reach other sandbox Pod IPs by default unless platform egress isolation is enforced; use a platform-level deny.always rule or an external CNI policy. The current egress sidecar's NAT interception is incompatible with gVisor; use Kata or CNI policy if both strong isolation and egress filtering are required. Docker mode does not provide the documented multi-tenant isolation. Pin images by digest and verify Cosign/provenance signatures. Only latest release/main receive security updates.
